reason: The bell detects low-pitched sounds: S3, S4 and the mid-diastolic rumble; opening snap and systolic clicks are high-pitched and best heard with the diaphragm.
Post-MI ventricular aneurysm shows a paradoxical precordial impulse, persistent ST elevation and an abnormal bulge of the cardiac silhouette; pulsus paradoxus suggests tamponade.
Rheumatic nodules are painless, 0.5-2 cm, over extensor bony prominences, and appear more than 3 weeks after other manifestations.
Carey Coombs murmur is a soft apical mid-diastolic murmur due to mitral valvulitis in acute rheumatic fever.
S2–OS interval shortens as stenosis worsens (higher LA pressure); OS is high-pitched (diaphragm), softens with calcification, and is best heard near apex/lower left sternal border.
Adenosine transiently blocks the AV node, terminating AV-node-dependent re-entry such as AVNRT; AF and flutter show only transient AV block, VT is usually unaffected.
MDI order: remove cap and shake, exhale and insert mouthpiece, tilt head back, slow deep inhalation while actuating, then 10-second breath-hold; only option C fits.
Of the options only low-dose ICS fits Step 1 (GINA: as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol or ICS with SABA); LTRA, LAMA or oral steroid add-ons belong to higher steps.
GOLD grading: FEV1/FVC <0.7 with FEV1 50-79% predicted is GOLD 2 (moderate); FEV1 70% is therefore moderate.
Protein ratio 0.08 and LDH ratio 0.33 with pH 7.6 indicate a transudate; myxoedema causes transudative effusion, while pancreatitis, sarcoidosis and rheumatoid arthritis cause exudates.
Gilbert syndrome: autosomal recessive UGT1A1 defect, isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia, no chronic liver disease stigmata; liver biopsy is unnecessary, so I, II and III are correct.
Acute nephritic syndrome causes haematuria, oliguria, oedema and hypertension; kidneys are normal-sized or enlarged, whereas bilaterally small kidneys indicate chronic kidney disease.
Hypothyroidism causes euvolaemic hyponatraemia; adrenocortical (mineralocorticoid) failure and burns cause hypovolaemic, and nephrotic syndrome hypervolaemic, hyponatraemia.
Type 2 reaction (ENL) is immune-complex (type III, Arthus-type) mediated; type 1 is the reversal reaction, leonine facies is lepromatous, and nasal involvement is early in LL.
Glossitis, diarrhoea and Casal necklace dermatitis indicate pellagra; maize (corn) diets cause it because its niacin is bound (niacytin) and tryptophan content is low.
Anagen is active growth, catagen the transitional (involution) phase and telogen the resting phase, so only statement I is correct.
OA commonly affects first MTP, PIP/DIP, knees, hips and lower cervical (C5–C6) and lumbar spine; the ankle is characteristically spared, so I, II and IV.
Classic heat stroke affects elderly sedentary patients, with respiratory alkalosis and usually no hyperkalaemia; marked lactic acidosis and hyperkalaemia typify exertional heat stroke.

Phenytoin (IgA deficiency/hypogammaglobulinaemia), severe malnutrition and nephrotic syndrome (urinary IgG loss) are classic secondary immunodeficiency causes; post-measles, not post-varicella, is the standard viral example.
Gluteal (not deltoid) injection reduces hepatitis B efficacy; two vaccines may share a thigh 1 inch apart; vaccine and immunoglobulin need separate sites.
Chloral hydrate is a classic radiopaque ingestion (CHIPES: chloral hydrate, heavy metals, iron, phenothiazines, enteric-coated, solvents); ethylene glycol is not radiopaque on abdominal films.
Prader-Willi and Angelman (15q11-q13) are classic imprinting disorders; Rubinstein-Taybi is a CREBBP mutation and Edwards is trisomy 18.
POCSO Section 9 makes disability, educational-institution staff and relatives aggravating; II, III and IV are correct, so C and D are both valid. Question was dropped.
Lap-feeding with mother's hand is IMNCI advice for 6-12 months; at 12-24 months: breastfeed on demand, family-pot food, 3-4 meals. Only option B excludes II.
Revised IMNCI/WHO 2014 (SAANS): vomiting everything (danger sign) and stridor in calm child mean severe pneumonia; fast breathing and chest indrawing are now 'pneumonia'.
IMNCI: tender swelling behind the ear is mastoiditis needing urgent referral; discharge <14 days is acute and >=14 days chronic ear infection.
Tuberous sclerosis and fragile X are the classic genetic syndromes associated with ASD; Patau syndrome is not.
CP is a permanent, non-progressive disorder of movement and posture from a lesion of the developing brain.
Modified Ashworth scale grades spasticity and GMFCS classifies motor severity in CP; MRC grades muscle power, Conners rates ADHD. D intended.
Methylphenidate (stimulant) and atomoxetine (non-stimulant noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor) treat ADHD; carbamazepine and clonazepam do not.
RBSK 'Deficiencies': anaemia, vitamin A deficiency, vitamin D deficiency (rickets), severe acute malnutrition and goitre; congenital hypothyroidism is listed separately, not as a deficiency.
Calcium stabilises the myocardium (I false) and beta-agonists shift potassium into cells (II false); insulin-glucose shifts potassium in and sodium polystyrene sulfonate removes it.
Rotavirus vaccines are stored at 2-8°C; prior intussusception is a contraindication; vaccination is deferred during acute gastroenteritis. I and III correct.
Tower of 3 cubes, running, domestic mimicry and a 10-word vocabulary are 18-month milestones.
Riding a tricycle, copying a circle and knowing own name and gender are 3-year milestones.
Term 2.8 kg baby: breastfeed within 1 hour, keep with mother, vitamin K 1 mg IM (0.5 mg only if <1000 g), full examination. I and IV correct.
Enteral topiramate (via nasogastric tube) is an established add-on in super-refractory status epilepticus; clonazepam, clobazam and lamotrigine are not standard SRSE options.
Benzodiazepine may be repeated once after 5 minutes at 0.1 mg/kg (lorazepam); midazolam infusion belongs to refractory SE. Only B avoids false statements II and III.
Central DI, high-solute boiled skimmed milk and osmotic diarrhoea from lactulose cause hypernatremia; Addison disease causes hyponatremia.
ET intubation allows control of inspiratory time and peak inspiratory (not expiratory) pressure, delivery of PEEP and protection against aspiration.
Hypomagnesemia and pseudohypoparathyroidism cause hypocalcemia; hyperphosphatemia (not hypophosphatemia) and alkalosis (not acidosis) lower ionized calcium.
Hand-arm vibration syndrome produces secondary Raynaud's phenomenon with episodic digital blanching, termed vibration white finger.
Screening needs an important, reasonably common disease with a recognisable early stage and an acceptable, sensitive, specific test; rarity of disease is not a criterion.
Hypercalcaemia with renal stones indicates primary hyperparathyroidism; sestamibi scintigraphy is the standard localisation study. Non-contrast CT has no role (4D-CT requires contrast).
Communicating hydrocephalus follows haemorrhage, meningitis or raised CSF protein impairing absorption; intraventricular lesions cause obstructive (non-communicating) hydrocephalus.
Direct spread from skull fracture or air-sinus infection is a recognised route (I true); viruses cause encephalitis, not abscess (IV false). Hence I, II and III.
Bilharzial pseudotubercles near the trigone/ureteric orifices are the earliest specific cystoscopic sign; sandy patches (calcified ova) appear later and are pathognomonic.
Craniosynostosis is premature suture fusion; skull growth perpendicular to the fused suture is restricted with compensatory parallel growth (Virchow's law).
Breast carcinoma is the commonest source of skeletal metastases in women and frequently produces lytic vertebral and rib deposits.
The sacrum is the commonest site of pressure ulcers, followed by heels and ischial tuberosities.
Proximal (jejunal) resection is best tolerated as ileum and colon compensate for water/sodium absorption; colectomy with ileostomy increases fluid and sodium loss. Source-dependent.
Serum lactate and base deficit reflect global tissue hypoperfusion and anaerobic metabolism and are standard resuscitation end-points.
Agenesis, Phrygian cap and floating gallbladder are classic congenital anomalies; 'Spigelian gallbladder' is not a recognised anomaly (Spigelian denotes caudate lobe or hernia).
BCS presents with abdominal pain, ascites and hepatomegaly; it results from hepatic vein thrombosis, mainly in young women, with caudate (segment 1) hypertrophy.
Splenic artery aneurysms are about four times commoner in women, usually saccular in the distal main trunk, multiple in only ~20%; trauma is not the usual cause.
Primary survey covers oxygenation/circulation and disability (GCS, pupils, glucose); mechanism of injury belongs to the history/secondary survey.
In ATLS, C is circulation with haemorrhage control; catastrophic external haemorrhage control is the separate <C> preceding A. Statements I, II, IV are correct.
Paediatric inguinal hernias are commoner in premature (not full-term) boys, essentially always indirect, need prompt repair and may transilluminate in infants; statement I is false.
Distal (glanular/coronal) hypospadias with the meatus just proximal to the glans is the commonest type; penoscrotal and perineal forms are rarer.
Minimal access surgery reduces heat loss, gives magnified vision and earlier mobility; incisional herniation is reduced, not increased.
Surgical texts commonly quote 3 mg/kg for plain lignocaine (7 mg/kg with adrenaline); anaesthesia/pharmacology texts quote about 4.5 mg/kg. Reference-dependent.
Lymphoedema causes swelling, aching or bursting pain, burning and cramps; swelling worsens with heat, so cold intolerance is not a typical symptom.
Chronic lymphoedema predisposes to lymphangiosarcoma, Kaposi sarcoma, squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma and lymphoma; leukaemia is not a recognised association.
Off-midline closure after pilonidal excision uses Limberg rhomboid flap, Z-plasty and Karydakis procedure; the flap used is V-Y advancement, not Y-V plasty.
A 3x4 cm tumour (>2 to <=5 cm) is T2; mobile ipsilateral level I axillary nodes are cN1; hence cT2N1Mx.
High-resolution manometry (Chicago classification) is the gold standard for diagnosing oesophageal motility disorders such as achalasia.
Plummer-Vinson: postcricoid web, iron-deficiency anaemia and dysphagia in middle-aged women, premalignant for postcricoid carcinoma; treatment is iron replacement and dilatation, not surgery.
Chadwick's (Jacquemier's) sign is the dusky hue of vestibule and anterior vaginal wall at about 8 weeks; B is Goodell's, C Hegar's, D Palmer's sign.
Duplicate of 24606: folic acid, penicillin prophylaxis and LMWH thromboprophylaxis are recommended in sickle cell pregnancy; azathioprine is not.

Indian texts list multiple pregnancy, previous caesarean and Rh isoimmunisation as ECV contraindications; gestation under 36 weeks is timing, not contraindication; references differ, so key D doubtful.
Thalassaemia trait shows microcytosis (low MCV, MCH) with raised HbA2 >3.5%; MCHC and TIBC are usually normal, distinguishing it from iron deficiency.
Hydroxychloroquine is safe in pregnancy and is continued as maintenance therapy for SLE, reducing flares; stopping it precipitates flares.
Wernicke's encephalopathy, jaundice with hepatic failure, hypoprothrombinaemia from vitamin K deficiency and convulsions are all recognised HG complications, so all four (A).

Severe perineal pain, rectal tenesmus/bearing down and urine retention after delivery are classic infralevator (vulval/paravaginal) hematoma features; supralevator hematoma presents with shock and abdominal/upper-vaginal mass.
Infants of diabetic mothers develop hypoglycaemia, hyperbilirubinaemia and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; calcium falls (hypocalcaemia), it does not rise. So I, III and IV (C).
HSG outlines the cavity and tubes: tubal patency after tuboplasty, synechiae, IUD localisation. A subserosal fibroid does not distort the cavity, so I, II and III (A).
CET replaces the dry bulb with a globe thermometer, covering air temperature, humidity, air velocity and mean radiant heat; sweat rate belongs to P4SR.
National Immunization Schedule footnotes: an unimmunised child can receive DPT up to 7 years and OPV up to 5 years of age.
Unvaccinated travellers from yellow fever areas are quarantined up to 6 days (incubation 3-6 days) from leaving the infected area (Park, IHR).
ASHA, not the ANM, is the main HBNC provider through home visits; statements I, III and IV are correct, so the answer is 'I, III and IV only'.
Octreotide runs 2-5 days, not 7; cyanoacrylate is glue obturation, not sclerotherapy; sclerotherapy controls ~90% of acute bleeds and all patients need secondary prophylaxis.
Systolic murmur at lower left sternal border increasing with inspiration (Carvallo sign), prominent CV wave in raised JVP and oedema indicate tricuspid regurgitation.
Nurturing Care Framework: good health, adequate nutrition, responsive caregiving, opportunities for early learning, security and safety = items 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 (option A).
LBW infants need oral iron 2 mg/kg/day until 12 months; the recommended vitamin D dose is 400 IU/day, not 200 IU.
Term IUGR/SGA babies commonly develop hypothermia, hypoglycemia and hypocalcemia, alongside polycythemia and perinatal asphyxia.
Term newborns lose up to about 10% of birth weight in the first week; regain is quoted from 10 days to 2 weeks, so A is safest.
Voluntary grasp is tested with a 1-inch cube; the dangling red ring tests visual following and reaching, and pellets test pincer grasp.
Urinary alkalinization aims for urine pH 7.5-8.5 while keeping blood pH below about 7.55.
Exchange transfusion is used for severe methemoglobinemia unresponsive to methylene blue; barbiturates, carbamazepine and theophylline are removed by MDAC, hemodialysis or hemoperfusion.
Antiepileptics like carbamazepine and phenobarbital are well adsorbed by charcoal; iron and lithium are not adsorbed and corrosives are a contraindication.
Angelman, fragile X and tuberous sclerosis are strongly associated with ASD; Williams syndrome is typified by hypersociability.
Neural tube closes by day 28; folic acid from at least 1 month before conception to 12 weeks prevents NTDs.
Historically type 3 (recipients) and type 2 (contacts) caused most VAPP; since the 2016 switch only bOPV types 1 and 3 can cause it. Era-dependent.
WHO revised IMCI: general danger signs (convulsions, unable to drink/feed) and stridor in a calm child define severe pneumonia/very severe disease; lower chest indrawing is now 'pneumonia'.
UIP: an unimmunised 11-month-old needs BCG (allowed up to 1 year), OPV, pentavalent (DPT+HepB), MR and others at one visit; no option includes both BCG and MR.
Haematuria with red cell casts indicates glomerular bleeding; haemoglobinuria and myoglobinuria give a heme-positive dipstick with no red cells (haemolysis, rhabdomyolysis).
Microaneurysms, dot-blot haemorrhages and neovascularization are classic fundoscopic DR signs; retinal thickening (macular oedema) needs stereoscopic/OCT assessment, though it is also a DR feature.
Thyroxine is needed after Sistrunk only when the excised thyroglossal tissue was the only functioning thyroid; option D states exactly this, a plain thyroglossal cyst does not.
Battle's sign (mastoid ecchymosis) indicates basal skull fracture involving the petrous temporal bone/middle cranial fossa.

Normal biomarkers with ST depression = unstable angina; antiplatelets plus anticoagulant (LMWH) is core therapy; thrombolysis contraindicated. Option A lacks anticoagulation and routine oxygen is not indicated.
Neonatal hypothyroidism (neonatal TSH) is the most sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency (Park); urinary iodine reflects recent intake. Stored explanation argues for D.

Crush-injury hyperkalaemia with wide QRS: calcium is not offered; sodium bicarbonate rapidly shifts potassium and treats rhabdomyolysis acidosis. Insulin needs glucose; procainamide and magnesium are inappropriate.

Tumour lysis syndrome: phosphate binders lower phosphate and rasburicase lowers urate (both indicated); hyperhydration at 2–4× maintenance without potassium is needed, so plain maintenance fluid is detrimental.
A, B and C are all true (coronal suture separates frontal and parietal bones; bregma diamond-shaped; frontal suture between frontal bones). The false statement must be missing option D.
Pancreatic pleural effusion is fluid in the pleural cavity; drainage is not always necessary (small effusions resolve; fistulas get thoracentesis/ERCP stenting). C is also arguable.
POSSUM needs operative variables (blood loss, peritoneal soiling, operative severity), so it is scored post-operatively; ASA, METs and RCRI are preoperative. Option D's end spilled into stem.

Fever, migratory large-joint polyarthritis, palpitations and prolonged PR fit Jones criteria for acute rheumatic fever; sore throat history is often absent. Enteric fever does not cause fleeting arthritis.
Rifampicin, a potent CYP2C9/3A4 inducer, accelerates warfarin metabolism and lowers INR, outweighing isoniazid's weak inhibition; warfarin effect decreases and dose needs increasing.
Wernicke triad is ataxia, ophthalmoplegia and encephalopathy (global confusion); retrograde and anterograde amnesia with confabulation characterise Korsakoff syndrome.
Copying milestones: circle 3 years, cross 4, square 4–4.5, triangle 5; the five-year milestone is triangle, while a circle is a three-year skill.
Bartholin's duct opens outside the hymen at the junction of anterior two-thirds and posterior one-third; the gland lies in the superficial perineal pouch. B is the false statement.
Bilateral ovarian tumour with capsule rupture and malignant ascites but no pelvic or peritoneal spread is FIGO stage IC, i.e. Stage I, not Stage III.
Stem is only ':' and the question depends on four unseen images to be sequenced; cannot be answered as stored.
Phrenicocolic ligament (sustentaculum lienis) supports the lower pole of the spleen and prevents its downward displacement.
The gag reflex needs both the glossopharyngeal afferent (IX) and the vagus efferent (X). IX is the conventional answer, but the stem does not say which limb.
Saphenous nerve accompanies the great saphenous vein in the leg; injury during vein harvest causes neuralgia over the medial leg and foot.
High K+ (140) with low Na+ (10) is intracellular fluid composition; interstitial fluid and ECF are sodium-rich. Embedded label and explanation also give ICF.
Leakage only on coughing or straining (raised intra-abdominal pressure) defines stress incontinence; urge incontinence follows sudden urgency from detrusor overactivity. Options C–D blank.
Xerophthalmia with keratomalacia (corneal softening) is characteristic of vitamin A deficiency.
In cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency cysteine cannot be made from methionine, so it becomes essential and is supplemented while methionine is restricted.
Keratan sulphate in the corneal stroma regulates collagen fibril spacing, maintaining corneal transparency.
HNPCC (Lynch syndrome) is caused by germline mismatch-repair gene defects (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2); MUTYH polyposis is a base-excision repair defect.
Tendon xanthomas with raised LDL-cholesterol = familial hypercholesterolaemia, Fredrickson type IIa. Type I has chylomicronaemia with eruptive xanthomas. Subject is biochemistry, not orthopaedics.
Mallory-Denk bodies in alcoholic liver disease are eosinophilic aggregates of intermediate filaments (cytokeratins 8/18) with ubiquitin and p62. Stored key 'F' invalid.
Beta2-microglobulin is the strongest prognostic marker in multiple myeloma (ISS with albumin); creatinine is a lesser factor. Embedded label and explanation also give C.
Migratory polyarthritis with carditis (mitral regurgitation) is acute rheumatic fever/rheumatic heart disease; biopsy shows Aschoff bodies, not infective endocarditis.
Pancytopenia with low reticulocytes, absent megakaryocytes, no immature cells and no organomegaly in a young adult means aplastic anaemia.
HNPCC (Lynch syndrome) is caused by germline defects in DNA mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), producing microsatellite instability.
CD10+, BCL2+ (t(14;18)) nodal lymphoma with cleaved/indented centrocytes and nucleolated centroblasts is follicular lymphoma; Burkitt is BCL2-negative.
Methotrexate acts mainly by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase; thymidylate synthase is the main target of 5-fluorouracil. Option D carries an 'Answer < A' artefact.
Rifampicin induces hepatic CYP enzymes, accelerating oestrogen/progestin metabolism and causing OCP failure; this is a pharmacology item filed under biochemistry.
Metronidazole produces a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, so alcohol is avoided during and for some days after therapy; ciprofloxacin is not contraindicated.
Topiramate is indicated for migraine prophylaxis and as adjunct therapy in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, so A and B are both correct; migraine is the intended answer.
Sibutramine and fenfluramine were withdrawn and metformin is not an anti-obesity drug; the empty option D probably held the intended answer, such as orlistat.

Anticholinergic toxidrome (dry hot skin, photophobia from mydriasis, urinary retention, restlessness) after fruit ingestion is Datura; physostigmine crosses the blood-brain barrier and is the antidote.
Putrefactive green discoloration and marbling are due to sulphmethaemoglobin; marbling appears around 36-48 h, not 24 h. Options C/D missing and image unseen.
Answer depends on the attached wound image, which cannot be viewed; incised-looking laceration is plausible but unverifiable.
Stored key 'E' invalid, option D empty, image unseen. For a pond-recovered body the finding likely reflects prolonged immersion (washerwoman/degloving skin), so C is probably intended.
Two ova of the same cycle fertilised by separate acts of coitus, possibly by different men, is superfecundation; superfetation involves different cycles.
Exposing oneself naked to unsuspecting strangers for sexual gratification is exhibitionism; voyeurism is gratification from secretly watching others undress or have sex.
Measles virus (Morbillivirus, Paramyxoviridae) is an enveloped, non-segmented, single-stranded negative-sense RNA virus.
Cream-filled pastries and custards are classic vehicles of S. aureus enterotoxin food poisoning; B. cereus is linked to fried rice. Microbiology, not forensic medicine.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an oxidase-positive pigment-producing obligate aerobe, is the classic invasive burn-wound pathogen. Microbiology rather than forensic medicine.
Under BMW Rules 2016, blood-soiled items such as cotton swabs and dressings go in the yellow category bag.
Diet lacking vegetables and fruit causes folate deficiency (stores last months); fast food still supplies animal-derived B12, whose stores last years.
Antibody excess (prozone) causes false-negative brucella agglutination in undiluted serum; dilution restores optimal proportions and a positive result.
Steroid-triggered hyperinfection with larvae in BAL, nocturnal cough and urticaria indicates Strongyloides stercoralis; option D holds only the answer label.
Stem is only a topic heading and all four options are empty.
Bloody diarrhoea suggests Shigella/Salmonella, for which selenite F broth is an enrichment medium; alkaline peptone water is for Vibrio and blood agar is not enrichment.
Leishmania (sandfly) and trypanosomes (tsetse fly) are both kinetoplastids, so the stem does not discriminate; sandfly likely intended (LD body), options C/D missing.
Streptococcus pneumoniae is the commonest cause of bacterial lobar pneumonia in HIV at any CD4 count; option D artefact and the explanation also name S. pneumoniae.
Blood spills are disinfected with sodium hypochlorite (0.5-1% available chlorine) after removing visible material.
Buboes indicate bubonic plague, transmitted by the rat flea Xenopsylla cheopis.
Under the BMW Rules 2016, microbiology culture waste and soiled cotton swabs go in the yellow bag after pre-treatment.
Under-five mortality is one of the four GHI indicators (with undernourishment, stunting and wasting), so stored key A cannot be the exception; options B-D are missing.
Koplik spots followed by rash = measles; measles virus (Paramyxoviridae, Morbillivirus) is enveloped with single-stranded negative-sense RNA.
Weight-for-age between median and -2SD is the normal zone on WHO/MCP growth charts, so reassure; NRC referral (embedded label D) is for severe acute malnutrition.
Height-for-age below -2 SD is stunting, reflecting chronic malnutrition; low weight-for-height (wasting) reflects acute malnutrition.
Pellagra (niacin deficiency) shows dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia; option A covers dietary history plus the other two Ds, so it is the best choice.
Recurrent candidal and viral infections from early infancy suggest a T-cell defect (e.g., SCID); live measles/MMR vaccine is contraindicated, whereas toxoids and killed vaccines are safe.
Under India's immunization schedule Td (formerly TT) is given at 10 and 16 years; BCG is given only at birth.
Encephalitis outbreak implies Japanese encephalitis; UIP uses live attenuated SA-14-14-2 JE vaccine, 0.5 ml subcutaneously at 9-12 and 16-24 months.
The Kata thermometer measures cooling power and low air velocities; the globe thermometer measures mean radiant temperature.
School health service is conventionally delivered at primary health centre level by the PHC medical officer and team; district is not the accepted answer.
India's National AQI: 201-300 poor, 301-400 very poor, 401-500 severe; an AQI of 470 is severe.
RR rising from 0.5 to 1.8 as CRP increases is a positive dose-response association: higher CRP, higher disease risk.

In Donabedian's structure–process–outcome evaluation, process evaluation assesses clinical management (diagnostic and treatment practices); input and structure denote resources, not management quality.
Purulent urethral discharge in a male is classic gonococcal urethritis. Chancroid and syphilis cause genital ulcers, and HIV does not cause discharge.
Cream pastries with vomiting within hours is classic S. aureus enterotoxin food poisoning; emetic B. cereus is linked to fried rice. Option D is an answer artefact.
VZV-seronegative means no prior infection, so she is susceptible to primary varicella (chickenpox); zoster is reactivation of latent virus and cannot occur.
When epistaxis fails packing and conservative care, endoscopic sphenopalatine artery ligation is the next step, before maxillary or external carotid ligation.
Persistent reactionary post-tonsillectomy bleeding in a child is managed in the OT under GA: remove the clot and ligate or coagulate the bleeding vessel.
CSOM with raised-ICP symptoms and ring lesion indicates otogenic brain abscess, commonest in temporal lobe; source label and explanation both say temporal abscess, not extradural.
Refractive surgery (ICL, LASIK) is not done at 15 years with unstable refraction; contact lenses (toric/RGP) are the alternative, presumably among missing options.
Stem stops before the actual question and all four options are empty.
Gradual painless visual loss in an elderly patient fits diabetic maculopathy with hard exudates; image unseen, and option D holds the answer label rather than option text.
Dry eyes, rough corneal surface and failing vision indicate vitamin A deficiency (xerophthalmia); retinoic acid, not iron, is intended. Option D carries an 'Answer <D' artefact.
Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency makes cysteine essential; treat with methionine restriction plus cysteine supplementation, pyridoxine and betaine.
Image shows a deficient eyelid (lid coloboma per explanation); chronic corneal exposure causes exposure keratitis, not cataract. Embedded answer label and explanation both state B.
Acute anterior uveitis in a young male with spinal radiograph findings is classic ankylosing spondylitis; the image is unseen but the clinical clue suffices.
Prostaglandin analogue latanoprost is first-line for POAG and avoids timolol-induced bronchospasm in asthmatics; gemeprost is an obstetric prostaglandin, not used in glaucoma.
Antiemetic (metoclopramide)-induced acute dystonia is treated with a central anticholinergic such as benzhexol, or promethazine/diphenhydramine.
Lobar consolidation in HIV: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause at all CD4 counts; Staph aureus is less frequent. Option D is empty.
Pure red cell aplasia with a mediastinal mass is a classic thymoma paraneoplastic association.
Stem truncated mid-sentence and all four options are empty.
CURB-65: age 68 (1) plus urea 44 mg/dl (about 7.3 mmol/L, above 7) (1) gives 2, warranting hospital ward admission.
pH 7.53 with pCO2 20 mmHg is respiratory alkalosis (HCO3 26 suggests added metabolic alkalosis); respiratory acidosis is wrong. Options C and D are empty.
The operative image is unseen; Thiersch anal encirclement is plausible, but Wells or Altemeier procedures cannot be excluded from text alone.
Lichtenstein tension-free mesh repair is the standard repair for adult direct inguinal hernia; herniotomy alone is not used for direct hernia. Bassini is an older alternative.
Options describe Fournier's gangrene: polymicrobial synergistic aerobic-anaerobic infection. Testes are spared and antigas-gangrene serum is not used, so A is true.
Hypotensive, tachycardic blunt abdominal trauma: FAST is the initial investigation (ATLS); CECT is reserved for haemodynamically stable patients.
Image unseen and options C–D blank; valvulae conniventes is an anatomical sign, not a condition; dilated loops showing them indicate small-bowel obstruction.
A twin delivery counts as one parity, so she is G2P1; neither G2P2 nor G2P3 is correct and the right option is missing.
Hysteroscopic septal resection (hysteroscopic metroplasty) is the treatment of choice for septate uterus; abdominal metroplasty largely abandoned. Question is gynaecology, not surgery.
Unruptured ectopic, hCG 2500, no cardiac activity: methotrexate (not listed) or surgery; expectant management needs hCG below about 1500 and falling. Salpingectomy is the acceptable listed option.
Only one option present. Active genital herpes in late pregnancy is managed with acyclovir and caesarean delivery, so A is the plausible intended answer.
Twins with different fathers arise from superfecundation: two ova of one cycle fertilised by separate acts of coitus.
Outflow obstruction from a transverse vaginal septum causes retrograde menstruation and early-onset endometriosis, giving dysmenorrhoea and chronic pelvic pain.
Profuse non-itchy discharge on day 12 in a woman trying to conceive is physiological ovulatory cervical mucus; no infective features described.
Warfarin is stopped at about 36 weeks and replaced with LMWH or unfractionated heparin before delivery; aspirin gives inadequate protection in mitral stenosis needing anticoagulation.
Normal calcium and PTH with low phosphate, high ALP and vitamin D resistance indicate hypophosphataemic rickets; VDDR types 1 and 2 show hypocalcaemia and raised PTH. Options C, D missing.
Height-for-age below -2 SD is stunting, an index of chronic malnutrition; weight-for-height below -2 SD (wasting) indicates acute malnutrition.
Only one option present. Webbed neck, short stature and low posterior hairline classically indicate Turner syndrome, although Noonan syndrome overlaps.
X-ray unseen and option D blank. Normal bone density excludes rickets and scurvy (both osteopenic), favouring metaphyseal dysplasia, which mimics rickets with normal mineralisation.

Posterior hip dislocation gives shortening with flexion, adduction and internal rotation; anterior gives abduction/external rotation; neck/IT fractures give external rotation. Explanation describes shoulder dislocation.
Non-foul, non-itchy profuse white discharge at day 13-15 (ovulation) is physiological cervical mucus, not candidiasis, BV or trichomoniasis.
Image unseen and option D blank; jejunum shows valvulae conniventes (stack-of-coins), ileum looks featureless; key Jejunum is plausible but the pattern shown cannot be verified.
Scurvy fits limb pain with normal Ca/P/ALP, unlike rickets, but scurvy causes osteopenia, contradicting 'normal BMD'; the answer hinges on the unseen X-ray.

Bergonie-Tribondeau law: radiosensitivity rises with mitotic activity and falls with differentiation, so neurons are least affected; spermatogonia are highly radiosensitive. Option D contains the answer.
