CAH (21-hydroxylase): 46,XX, Barr body positive, basal 17-OHP >800 ng/dL diagnostic; testosterone >200 ng/dL points to an androgen-secreting tumour. Statement numbering garbled.
Turner syndrome has streak ovaries with raised FSH/LH, i.e. hypergonadotropic, not hypogonadotropic, hypogonadism.
Kallmann syndrome: GnRH deficiency with anosmia, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and primary amenorrhoea; GnRH is low, not elevated.
Positive DPL: RBC >100,000/mm3, WBC >500/mm3, raised lavage amylase, bile, bacteria or food fibres; WBC >100 is not a criterion.
Stored key blank; stem pastes several questions and option C holds another item. Felty's splenectomy gives only transient improvement, so statements 1,2,3 (inline code a) are correct.
Paediatric inguinal hernia is commoner in preterm infants (I false); it is indirect (patent processus vaginalis), needs prompt repair, and may transilluminate in infants.
Scratch drawing blood is a transdermal Category III exposure: wash wound, give anti-rabies vaccine plus rabies immunoglobulin. Community medicine item filed under General Surgery.
Park: incidence guides control action, rising incidence suggests programme failure, and fluctuation suggests a change in aetiology; all three statements are correct.

All four codes crammed into option A; B-D empty. Warthin's tumour: second commonest benign salivary tumour, older men, almost only parotid, bilayered oncocytic epithelium in lymphoid stroma: all true.
POSSUM combines 12 physiological and 6 operative variables; anaesthetic dosage and wound status are not included. All four codes crammed into option A; B-D empty.
All four codes merged into option A; B-D empty. ASA E denotes emergency, not elective, so statement 4 is false; intended answer is 1, 2 and 3 (A).
Eyelid BCC is the commonest eyelid malignancy, favours the lower lid, rarely metastasises, and extensive lesions need Mohs micrographic excision.
Fibroids are the commonest benign solid tumour in women, peak at 35-45 years, asymptomatic ones are observed; nulliparity, not multiparity, increases risk.
Extension to uterus and tubes without extrapelvic peritoneal implants or nodes is FIGO stage IIA; malignant ascites alone does not upstage to III.
Closed os, no pain or bleeding, uterus smaller than dates and absent cardiac activity indicate missed abortion; inevitable/incomplete abortion have an open os with bleeding.
Sagittal suture lies between the parietal bones; coronal separates frontal and parietal, the frontal suture lies between frontal bones, posterior fontanelle is triangular.
Puerperal psychosis has abrupt onset usually within the first few days (about 4) postpartum, mostly with past/family history; recurrence is well below 60%; ECT is for refractory cases.
Options A–C empty, their text merged into stem. WIF −15 to −25°C for OPV and ILR 8-hour supply are true; WICs are state/regional, so '1, 2 and 4' intended.
Options A-C sit in the stem. Solid-fuel reduction is India's added tenth national NCD target, not a WHO global target; correct is 1, 2 and 3 only (B), not D.
Options A-C sit in the stem; only D present. AMB: 3-point yearly reduction, 6x6x6 strategy, biweekly IFA syrup at 6-59 months, 180 IFA doses each in pregnancy and lactation.
ASHAs find suspected leprosy cases and ensure MDT completion; RCS incentive and MCR footwear are programme provisions, not ASHA tasks: 1 and 2 only. Options A-C sit in stem.
Older Indian texts name gonococcus; current literature (Williams, Novak) describes Bartholin abscess as polymicrobial with E. coli the commonest isolate, gonococcus uncommon.
Levator ani (as described in DC Dutta) comprises pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus and ischiococcygeus; obturator internus, piriformis, bulbospongiosus and ischiocavernosus are not parts of it.
DeLancey level I (uterosacral-cardinal suspension) defects cause uterovaginal/vault prolapse and enterocele; level II causes cystocele/rectocele; level III perineal/urethral defects.

Pelvic cellular tissue supports organs, sheaths vessels and ureter, spreads infection and hypertrophies in pregnancy; being the primary lymphatic route for cervical cancer is not a listed significance.
Radical hysterectomy divides the paracervical plexus and its sacral connections, causing marked bladder atonia; simple hysterectomy rarely does.
Gartner's duct is the persistent caudal remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, giving Gartner's cysts in the anterolateral vaginal wall.
Genital tubercle forms clitoris, urogenital folds labia minora, labioscrotal swellings labia majora; Mullerian ducts form tubes, uterus and upper vagina.
Bartholin's (greater vestibular) glands arise from urogenital sinus endoderm, homologous to male bulbourethral glands.
Imperforate hymen is failure of disintegration of central cells of the Mullerian eminence; failed sinovaginal bulb canalization causes vaginal atresia, failed septal resorption septate uterus.
Retained menses first distend the vagina (haematocolpos), then the uterus (haematometra), then the tubes (haematosalpinx).
Imperforate hymen is treated by cruciate incision (hymenotomy) with drainage of retained blood; metroplasty is for septate/bicornuate uterus.
Unicornuate uterus results from arrested development of one paramesonephric duct; didelphys from non-fusion, septate/arcuate from failed septal resorption.
Idiopathic/constitutional causes account for most (about 80-90%) central precocious puberty in girls; McCune-Albright and granulosa cell tumour are GnRH-independent.
Continuous long-acting GnRH agonists (leuprolide, goserelin, triptorelin) desensitise the pituitary and are the treatment of choice for central precocious puberty.
Puberty menorrhagia requires exclusion of bleeding disorders, especially von Willebrand disease and ITP, the commonest haematological causes.
Turner syndrome (45,XO gonadal dysgenesis) causes primary ovarian failure with raised FSH/LH; constitutional delay, Kallmann and craniopharyngioma are hypogonadotropic.
Menopause is permanent cessation of menstruation from loss of ovarian follicular activity, diagnosed retrospectively after 12 (not 6) months of amenorrhoea.
WHO densitometric criteria: T-score between -1.0 and -2.5 is osteopenia (low bone mass); -2.5 or lower is osteoporosis.
AMH is secreted by granulosa cells of growing preantral/small antral follicles and fetal Sertoli cells; 'primordial' wording is imprecise but option B is clearly intended.
Kisspeptin from hypothalamic neurons acts on GPR54 (KISS1R) to stimulate GnRH release and is key to the onset of puberty.
Normal menstrual flow lasts about 4–5 days (normal range roughly 2–7 days), with an average blood loss of about 35 mL.
A is standard: estradiol >200 pg/mL for ~48–50 h triggers the LH surge. The explanation also calls B true, but the surge lasts ~48 h. C and D are false.
The endometrium is thickest in the secretory phase (~12–14 mm). Option C also contains the giveaway word 'highest'.
The proliferative phase runs from day 5/6 (end of menses) to ovulation on day 14 of a 28-day cycle.
Luteal-phase progesterone keeps the internal os tightly closed with thick, viscid mucus. A funnel-shaped os is an estrogenic (follicular-phase) feature.
Ferning reflects the high-NaCl, low-protein mucus produced under the preovulatory estrogen peak. Progesterone abolishes it.
The preovulatory estrogen peak gives a clean smear dominated by superficial cornified cells with pyknotic nuclei. Navicular/intermediate cells are a progestational pattern.
Post-ovulatory progesterone abolishes ferning, so its disappearance after day 21–22 is presumptive evidence of ovulation. Persistent ferning suggests anovulation.
The corpus luteum functions for about 14 ± 2 days (12–14 days) and regresses unless hCG rescues it.
Starting age depends on the guideline: ACOG/USPSTF say 21, ACS 2020 says 25, WHO 2021 and GOI say 30. Option C matches Indian texts; B matches ACOG.
Endometrial sampling is indicated for DUB/AUB, postmenopausal bleeding and infertility work-up including endometrial TB. Polyps need hysteroscopy; blind sampling misses them.
Leptin from adipose tissue signals body fat stores to the hypothalamus, linking body composition with the H-P-O axis, menarche and menstrual cyclicity.
Standard sequence after Marshall and Tanner: growth acceleration, breast budding, pubic/axillary hair, peak height velocity, then menarche.
A nullipara has never carried a pregnancy to viability, though she may have aborted. A nulligravida has never conceived; a primigravida is pregnant for the first time.
Physiological edema is slight, confined to the ankles, relieved by rest and has no proteinuria. Facial edema or proteinuria points to preeclampsia or disease.
Korotkoff phase V (disappearance of sounds) is recommended for diastolic BP in pregnancy. Phase IV is used only if sounds persist to zero.
DC Dutta starts iron from 16 weeks. Indian programmes say after the first trimester (14–16 weeks, or the 4th month); WHO says as early as possible.
Antenatal care is the strategy and intranatal care the tactic, so statement 3 is false; 1, 2 and 4 are true. The stem lost its '4.' label.
Preconceptional counselling is recommended for all couples planning a pregnancy, not only for complicated cases.
In normal pregnancy the umbilical artery S/D ratio, PI and RI fall as gestation advances, so statement 4 is false; statements 1–3 are correct.
MMR is a live attenuated vaccine and is contraindicated in pregnancy. Hepatitis B, rabies vaccine and tetanus toxoid are safe.
The umbilical vein is larger and causes less bradycardia (arterial spasm) and less bleeding. Oxygenated blood is true but not a reason. The stem cites 'notes' that aren't given.
Lightening is descent of the presenting part into the pelvis 2–3 weeks before labour in primigravidae. It eases breathlessness and increases micturition.
Friedman's active phase has acceleration, maximum slope and deceleration phases. Expulsion belongs to the second stage.
Mechanism of labour: engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation, crowning, extension, restitution, external rotation, expulsion.
The puerperium is the 6 weeks after delivery, during which the genital organs return to the non-pregnant state.
Late decelerations (onset >20 s after the contraction starts, uniform) reflect uteroplacental insufficiency. Cord compression causes variable decelerations.
WHO 2018: the active first stage usually does not exceed 12 hours in first labours or 10 hours in subsequent labours.
WHO defines abortion as expulsion or extraction of an embryo or fetus weighing 500 g or less.
Autosomal trisomies (trisomy 16 the commonest) make up about half of abnormal karyotypes in miscarriages. 45,X is the single commonest specific anomaly.
Complete miscarriage: uterus smaller than period of amenorrhoea, firmer, closed os, trace bleeding; open os with palpable products indicates inevitable/incomplete miscarriage.
Current ASRM/ESHRE definition is two or more pregnancy losses; option C is self-labelled 'earlier definition', so 'currently defined' points to B, not both.
Standard APLA regimen in recurrent miscarriage: low-dose aspirin plus prophylactic heparin 5,000 units SC twice daily until about 34 weeks; warfarin is teratogenic.
History-indicated (prophylactic) cerclage is done around 14 weeks, or at least 2 weeks before the earliest previous loss, after confirming viability.
Key reflects MTP Act 1971 (20 weeks; two RMPs for 12-20 weeks); 2021 amendment needs one RMP to 20 weeks, two for 20-24 weeks, so no option fits current law.
Anencephaly is a lethal anomaly incompatible with life, justifying termination irrespective of gestational age (substantial fetal abnormality).
About 50% of first-trimester miscarriages are chromosomally abnormal, autosomal trisomy being the commonest; chromosomal anomaly is the leading cause.
Tubal pregnancies form about 95-97% of ectopics and the ampulla is the commonest site, followed by isthmus.
Commonest characteristic TVS finding of unruptured tubal ectopic is an inhomogeneous adnexal mass separate from the ovary (blob sign); ring of fire is nonspecific (corpus luteum too).
Spiegelberg criteria: intact ipsilateral tube, sac in ovarian position, sac connected to uterus by the ovarian ligament (not round ligament), ovarian tissue in sac wall.
Heterotopic pregnancy is the coexistence of an intrauterine and an extrauterine pregnancy, commoner after assisted reproduction.
GTD classification lists hydatidiform mole, invasive mole, choriocarcinoma, PSTT and ETT; a tubal site is not a separate category, though tubal choriocarcinoma is still choriocarcinoma.
Complete mole shows a snowstorm (vesicular) pattern without fetus; ring of fire suggests ectopic/corpus luteum, twin peak indicates dichorionic twins.
High-risk factors for post-molar GTN: hCG >100,000 mIU/mL, age >40, uterus >20 weeks size, theca lutein cysts >6 cm; other options are low-risk values.
Current advice is to avoid conception for 6 months after hCG normalises following molar evacuation; one year was the older recommendation.
Cannon-ball lung opacities in GTD denote pulmonary metastases of persistent trophoblastic neoplasia; other options are unrelated.
Dizygotic (binovular) twins are the commoner type, conventionally about 80% of twins in Indian obstetric texts; monozygotic about 20%.
Splitting at days 4-8 (after inner cell mass forms, before amnion) gives monochorionic diamniotic twins, the commonest monozygotic type.
Twin peak (lambda) sign indicates dichorionic diamniotic twins; T sign indicates monochorionic diamniotic twins.
Superfecundation is fertilisation of two ova of the same cycle by separate coital acts; superfetation involves ova from different cycles.
Sonographic polyhydramnios: AFI of 24-25 cm or more, or single deepest vertical pocket of 8 cm or more.
Renal agenesis (Potter sequence) is a fetal cause; dehydration and hypertension are maternal, uteroplacental insufficiency is placental.
Battledore placenta means marginal cord insertion; velamentous insertion is into the membranes.
Lambda (twin-peak) sign, chorionic tissue projecting into the base of the inter-twin membrane, denotes dichorionic diamniotic twins; T-sign denotes monochorionic diamniotic.
Placenta previa is not a risk factor (linked to lower pre-eclampsia risk); primigravidity, hyperplacentosis such as molar pregnancy, and thrombophilias are risk factors.
HELLP complicates about 10-20% of severe pre-eclampsia; it can occur without hypertension, MAHA is its hallmark, and hepatic haematoma is usually diagnosed by CT.
In an eclamptic fit the violent jaw movements of the clonic stage cause tongue bite; tonic stage shows tongue protrusion, apnoea and cyanosis.
Magnesium sulphate (Pritchard or Zuspan regimen) is the anticonvulsant of choice for prevention and treatment of eclampsia.
Gestational hypertension: new BP of 140/90 or more after 20 weeks without proteinuria, resolving within 12 weeks postpartum.
ACE inhibitors are fetotoxic (renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia) and contraindicated; labetalol, nifedipine and methyldopa are standard in pregnancy.
Haematuria or RBC casts with raised creatinine indicate intrinsic renal disease rather than pure pre-eclampsia; option D and explanation carry an import artefact sentence.
Ventouse is contraindicated below 34 weeks (scalp and intracranial haemorrhage risk); unengaged head, CPD and refusal contraindicate both instruments.
Internal podalic version is contraindicated in neglected obstructed labour even with a living fetus (risk of uterine rupture); its main indication is transverse lie of the second twin.

Craniotomy is used for obstructed cephalic labour with a dead fetus, hydrocephalus even if the fetus is living, and interlocked twins. Neglected shoulder with dead fetus and accessible neck calls for decapitation.

Cleidotomy (dividing the clavicles) is a destructive operation that reduces shoulder girth in shoulder dystocia with a dead fetus. Option B matches the standard indication, though the anencephaly qualifier is oddly worded.
DC Dutta defines caesarean section as delivery through abdominal and uterine incisions after 28 completed weeks; before that, the same operation is called hysterotomy.
WHO/ICD definition: death while pregnant or within 42 days of termination, irrespective of duration and site, from causes related to or aggravated by pregnancy.

Indian MNM-Review guidelines require at least one criterion each from clinical findings, investigations and interventions (minimum three). WHO near-miss criteria differ: any single criterion qualifies.
Perinatal mortality = fetal deaths of 1000 g or more (28 weeks or more) plus early neonatal deaths in the first 7 days. Option D contains import debris.
Folic acid deficiency is a cause of abruptio placentae. Maternal age over 35, a uterine scar and smoking are recognised risk factors for placenta previa.
Type II (marginal) previa: the placenta reaches the margin of the internal os without covering it. Type III covers it partially and Type IV completely.
Expectant (Macafee) management requires gestation under 37 weeks, no active bleeding, a stable mother and assured fetal well-being. Active bleeding is an indication for delivery.
Couvelaire uterus (uteroplacental apoplexy) is blood extravasated into the myometrium. It is recognised at laparotomy and is typical of severe concealed abruptio placentae.
In the clinical grading of abruption, Grade 3 means marked uterine tenderness, pronounced shock and fetal death, with a possible coagulation defect.
The Apt (alkali denaturation) test finds fetal haemoglobin in vaginal blood, confirming bleeding from torn fetal vessels in vasa previa. Kleihauer-Betke measures fetomaternal haemorrhage.
A is true (concealed type). R correctly describes revealed abruption, so by strict assertion-reason logic both are true but R doesn't explain A (B); the key treats R as false.
Lower limit of physiological anaemia: Hb 10 g%, RBC 3.2 million/mm3, PCV 32%, with normal RBC morphology. MCHC below 30% indicates iron deficiency.
DC Dutta calls MCHC (below 30%) the most sensitive index of iron deficiency anaemia in pregnancy. General haematology texts regard ferritin and iron studies as earlier markers.
After a previous NTD-affected infant, give 4 mg folic acid daily from one month before conception through the first trimester; 400 micrograms is the routine dose.

Penicillin prophylaxis is recommended, not contraindicated, in sickle cell disease, so only option B leaves out statement 2. Hydroxyurea stops 3 months before conception; vaginal delivery is preferred.
Carrier x normal: 50% of offspring are carriers (thalassaemia minor) and 50% normal. The explanation's '25% normal' is wrong, but the key of 50% is correct.
Repeated transfusions iron-overload patients with thalassaemia major, so oral and parenteral iron are contraindicated; transfusion and folic acid are given.
Gestational thrombocytopenia is a mild fall below 150,000/microL, usually staying above 70,000, without fetal thrombocytopenia; it rarely needs treatment.
Clark/ACOG Group 3 (25-50% mortality): pulmonary hypertension, coarctation with valvular involvement, Marfan with aortic involvement. MS with AF and uncorrected Fallot are Group 2.
Peripartum cardiomyopathy: failure from the last month of pregnancy to 5 months postpartum, no prior heart disease, EF below 45% (not above 50%), LVEDD above 2.7 cm/m2.
Combined pills are avoided in significant heart disease because oestrogen raises thromboembolic risk: the assertion is false and the reason true. Option C has a stray backslash.
GDM risk markers include unexplained perinatal loss, persistent glycosuria, polyhydramnios and a previous baby of 4 kg or more. A 2.5 kg birthweight is not a risk factor.
Overt diabetes in pregnancy (ADA/IADPSG): fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL or more, HbA1c of 6.5% or more, or random glucose of 200 mg/dL or more.
The two-step strategy uses a 50 g non-fasting glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks, regardless of time of day or last meal.
Infants of diabetic mothers develop hypoglycaemia, RDS, polycythaemia, hyperbilirubinaemia and hypocalcaemia, not hypercalcaemia.
First-trimester methimazole/carbimazole is linked to embryopathy (aplasia cutis, choanal or oesophageal atresia), so PTU is preferred in the first trimester.
Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy: palm and sole pruritus, oestrogen-related cholestasis, raised bile acids. Liver biopsy shows cholestasis without necrosis, so statement 3 is false.
UDCA is first-line for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy; it enhances biliary bile acid excretion and relieves pruritus. Cholestyramine is a less effective adjunct.
Lamotrigine (like levetiracetam) carries the lowest major malformation risk; valproate, phenytoin and phenobarbital are clearly more teratogenic.
Anti-Sm is the most SLE-specific antibody offered; nephritis/activity correlation is classically anti-dsDNA (not listed). Anti-Ro/La relate to neonatal lupus, aPL to thrombosis and fetal loss.
Rifampicin induces hepatic CYP enzymes, accelerating contraceptive steroid metabolism and causing OC failure; OCs are unreliable with rifampicin, so A false, R true.
Primary, secondary or early latent syphilis in pregnancy: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose; penicillin is the only adequate therapy in pregnancy.
Malaria causes metabolic (lactic) acidosis, not alkalosis; anaemia (haemolytic, megaloblastic from folate depletion), hypoglycaemia and DIC are maternal effects, so 1, 3 and 4.
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: at least 10^5 CFU/mL of a single species in clean-catch midstream urine, ideally on two samples, without urinary symptoms.
Live attenuated vaccines (MMR, varicella) are contraindicated in pregnancy; inactivated influenza and hepatitis B vaccines are safe and given when indicated.
Planned CS at 38 weeks when viral load exceeds threshold (>50 copies/mL in RCOG/BHIVA-based teaching; current BHIVA >=400, ACOG >1000); vaginal delivery if <50.
Red degeneration occurs in the second half of pregnancy or puerperium (A false); it is an aseptic haemorrhagic infarction, infection plays no role (R true). Stem has junk audit text.
Oxytocin is synthesised in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus and transported along axons to the posterior pituitary for release.
Water intoxication is an oxytocin (ADH-like) effect; ergometrine causes nausea, vomiting, hypertension, peripheral vasospasm/gangrene and suppression of lactation.
Prophylactic ergometrine is avoided in suspected twins, pre-eclampsia, heart disease and Rh-negative mothers; atonic PPH is a therapeutic indication, not a contraindication.
PGF2-alpha (carboprost) is a potent bronchoconstrictor and is contraindicated in asthma; PGE1 and PGE2 are not bronchoconstrictors.
Ergometrine is contraindicated for labour acceleration (oxytocin is used); methergine arrests post-abortal bleeding; misoprostol (PGE1) is an accepted AMTSL agent, though oxytocin is first choice.
ACOG/ISSHP list labetalol, nifedipine and methyldopa all as first-line; NICE prefers labetalol then nifedipine. B is the traditional textbook answer, but A is equally defensible.
FDA category D: positive evidence of human fetal risk, but benefits may justify use in serious disease; category X is when risk clearly outweighs any benefit.
Pudendal block is given with lignocaine (or chloroprocaine), not bupivacaine, so A is false; bupivacaine's cardiotoxicity limits its obstetric use (e.g., paracervical block), so R true.
Megaloblastic anaemia is macrocytic (MCV >100 fL) with normal MCHC; iron deficiency is microcytic hypochromic with low MCV and low MCHC.
All HIV-exposed neonates receive ARV prophylaxis within hours of birth irrespective of feeding; other options withhold it. The drug (nevirapine or zidovudine) and duration vary by guideline.
Primary pulmonary hypertension, Eisenmenger syndrome and pulmonary veno-occlusive disease carry prohibitive maternal mortality, warranting early termination; NYHA I mitral stenosis is low risk.
Parvovirus B19 (erythema infectiosum) gives the slapped-cheek rash and fetal anaemia/hydrops; Clutton joints, saber shins and Hutchinson teeth are late congenital syphilis.
A 200 mg dried ferrous sulphate tablet supplies about 60-65 mg elemental iron, the standard daily prophylactic dose in pregnancy.
Hospitalisation is advised at an arbitrary Hb of about 7.5 g/dL (severe anaemia) for evaluation, parenteral iron or transfusion; higher levels are managed as outpatients.
Sickle cell labour: oxygen to keep saturation >94%, regional anaesthesia, antibiotic cover; adequate hydration is essential since dehydration precipitates sickling, so fluid restriction is wrong.
Stem garbled (statements 2-3 merged; '<40% Mitral valve area >' lost) and states the answer. CARPREG predictors: NYHA >II, LVEF <40%, MVA <2 cm2, prior TIA/stroke.
Macrosomia is common in diabetic pregnancy (A true); it results from fetal hyperinsulinaemia secondary to maternal hyperglycaemia (Pedersen hypothesis), not cortisol blocking insulin (R false).
Hydroxychloroquine is an antimalarial safe in pregnancy and the standard maintenance therapy for SLE, reducing flares and steroid requirement; artesunate, quinine and mefloquine have no SLE role.
Late congenital syphilis (after 2 years): Hutchinson teeth, saber shins, Clutton joints; maculopapular rash is an early manifestation.
Page grade 1 abruption: slight bleeding, irritable uterus, maternal BP and fibrinogen unaffected, good fetal heart. Option D contains junk audit-log text.
Plasma volume rises ~40-50% against red cell mass ~20-30%, causing haemodilution; physiological anaemia is normocytic normochromic, so statement 4 is false and only A excludes it.
Ursodeoxycholic acid is first-line but not offered; cholestyramine, a bile-acid binding resin, is the listed drug used to relieve the pruritus of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy.
WHO advises HIV-positive mothers in resource-limited settings to breastfeed exclusively for 6 months with ARV cover; mixed feeding raises transmission risk.
Methotrexate, mifepristone and alcohol are classic FDA category X; ACE inhibitors were really C/D and letter categories were retired in 2015, but X is clearly intended.
Lignocaine has rapid onset and intermediate duration; bupivacaine has slow onset and long duration, so pairs 1 and 4 are correct.
Stem truncated after 'Cervical length', so statements 2-4 are lost; intended answer: fFN and cervicovaginal cytokines are biochemical predictors, cervical length is biophysical.
Prolonged rupture of membranes means membranes ruptured more than 24 hours before delivery; options A and B define preterm PROM and term PROM.
Amniotic fluid (pH 7-7.5) is alkaline versus acidic vaginal secretions (pH 4.5-5.5); nitrazine turns blue above pH ~6, so R explains A.
Post-term neonates suffer meconium aspiration, polycythaemia and hypoglycaemia; intraventricular haemorrhage is characteristic of prematurity, not post-maturity.
Anencephaly (absent pituitary/adrenal hypoplasia) is the fetal factor; placental sulfatase deficiency is classed as placental, wrong dates and primiparity as other/maternal factors.
Spalding sign is irregular overlapping of fetal skull bones on X-ray about 7 days after death; gas in heart and great vessels is Robert's sign.
Scar rupture features: abnormal CTG, scar pain, shoulder-tip/chest pain, sudden breathlessness, cessation of previously efficient contractions; increasing contraction intensity is not a feature.
Classical/inverted-T incision, prior uterine rupture and placenta praevia contraindicate TOLAC; a single previous lower segment caesarean is the usual VBAC candidate.
Only IgG is actively transported across the placenta via neonatal Fc receptors; IgM is too large, so IgG anti-D causes haemolytic disease of the fetus.
D antigen causes most Rh disease, the RH locus lies on chromosome 1p, and MCA-PSV Doppler has replaced Liley's chart, so statement 4 is false.
Anti-D given within 72 hours clears fetal D-positive cells from maternal circulation before primary immunisation occurs; R correctly explains A.
300 µg anti-D neutralises about 30 mL fetal whole blood (15 mL fetal red cells); larger bleeds need Kleihauer-quantified additional doses.
Stem garbled by stripped '<' text; statements merged/missing. Intended: high cord bilirubin, low cord Hb, bilirubin rising >1 mg/dL/h and TSB >=20 are indications; statement 4 is not.
Normal fasting homocysteine is about 5-15 µmol/L; hyperhomocysteinaemia is variably defined (>12 or >15 µmol/L); >12 is the only listed option matching standard cut-offs.
Inlet contraction: obstetric conjugate <10 cm, transverse <12 cm or diagonal conjugate below ~11.5 cm; intertuberous diameter <=8 cm defines outlet contraction, so statement 4 is excluded.
Constriction ring is incoordinate uterine action, may occur in any stage, is not felt abdominally and never causes rupture; an abdominally palpable oblique groove is the retraction ring.
Bandl's retraction ring follows obstructed labour and rises progressively; a constriction ring stays fixed, is not palpable and never ruptures. Option D carries import residue text.
Term PROM is rupture after 37 weeks before labour; vaginal pH in pregnancy is 4.5-5.5 (amniotic fluid 7-7.5); nitrazine turns blue above pH 6; ferning confirms.
Maternal factors in post-term pregnancy are primiparity, previous post-term pregnancy, sedentary habit and elderly multiparity; pre-eclampsia instead leads to earlier, often preterm, delivery.
IUFD X-ray signs: Spalding sign (~7 days), Robert's sign (gas in heart/great vessels, earliest), crowding of ribs and hyperflexion, not hyperextension, of the spine.
Severe suprapubic pain or scar tenderness persisting between contractions is an early clinical sign of scar dehiscence or rupture, which is why it is concerning.
Inverted-T incision, previous uterine rupture and placenta praevia contraindicate trial of labour; one prior lower segment caesarean is not a contraindication.
Android pelvis: heart-shaped/triangular inlet, convergent side walls, prominent ischial spines, narrow sacrosciatic notch and narrow subpubic angle.
Rachitic flat pelvis is reniform, osteomalacic pelvis triradiate; Naegele's pelvis lacks one sacral ala and Robert's pelvis lacks both, so statements 3 and 4 are swapped.
Triple descending gradient: wave starts at cornual pacemaker and spreads downward, intensity and duration both decreasing away from it; statement 3 is false, only B excludes it.
Constriction ring is localized incoordinate spasm, can occur in any stage, uterus never ruptures; R describes Bandl's (pathological retraction) ring of obstructed labour, so R false.
Anthropoid pelvis, high pelvic inclination, primary brachycephaly and anterior (not posterior) wall placenta predispose to occipito-posterior position.
Pinard's brings down legs (frank to footling), Lovset delivers extended arms, Burns-Marshall the aftercoming head; Zavanelli is cephalic replacement for shoulder dystocia.
Shoulder dystocia cannot be reliably predicted or prevented by ultrasound, so statement 1 is false; only option excluding it is 2, 3 and 4.
Both true (4 mg periconceptional folate for NTD prevention, mainly recurrence; anencephaly = absent vault and brain with normal face), but R only describes morphology, not folate's effect.
Standard Dutta definition: >500 mL after vaginal birth or any loss impairing general condition; option D resembles ACOG's >=1000 mL definition, creating some ambiguity.
AMTSL reduces PPH by about 60%; continuing oxytocin infusion for an hour after induced/augmented labour is a separate preventive measure, not the explanation.
Absence of Nitabuch's layer is the histopathological basis of accreta, not a sonographic sign; loss of retroplacental clear zone and bladder-serosa disruption are USG signs.
Recession of presenting part, cessation of contractions and easily palpable fetal parts with absent FHS indicate rupture; fever with foul lochia indicates puerperal sepsis.
Lactational mastitis typically begins in the second to fourth postpartum week, rarely within the first week.
Blues affects about half of women and has no specific metabolic/endocrine abnormality; the second statement does not explain its frequency.
Dopaminergic ergot derivatives (bromocriptine, cabergoline) inhibit prolactin and suppress lactation; frequent suckling raises prolactin and promotes milk production.
A large anterior fontanelle suggests hypothyroidism (also Down syndrome, osteogenesis imperfecta), not hyperthyroidism, which causes early closure.
Umbilical artery Doppler predicts fetal acidosis in FGR and absent/reversed end-diastolic flow prompts delivery; brain sparing is an MCA finding.
Intact membranes characterise scar dehiscence; true scar rupture involves the whole scar, ruptured membranes, continuity with peritoneal cavity and bleeding.
Infectious mastitis (Thomsen criteria): milk leukocytes >10^6/mL with bacteria >10^3/mL.
Mastitis is usually due to penicillinase-producing Staphylococcus aureus; dicloxacillin (or flucloxacillin) is the drug of choice, erythromycin if penicillin-allergic.
Both statements are accepted textbook facts (abrupt onset within days; recurrence about 20-25%); recurrence risk does not explain timing of onset.
Postpartum psychosis is a psychiatric emergency needing admission and antipsychotic therapy; lithium is not universal first-line and breastfeeding is not always advisable.
Postpartum depression affects 10-20% with gradual onset and high recurrence; 50% prevalence and reassurance-only fit blues, sudden onset fits psychosis.
Fetal abdominal circumference (reflecting liver glycogen) is the single most sensitive biometric parameter for detecting FGR.
Placental insufficiency diverts blood away from fetal kidneys, so oligohydramnios is frequent in FGR but not invariable.
Preterm neonates classically develop hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, ROP and PDA; hyperglycaemia is not a classical listed complication (though it occurs in ELBW infants).
Supplemental oxygen in preterms is kept low (traditionally <=35%) to avoid retinopathy; quick cord clamping is an older teaching now replaced by delayed clamping.
Placenta previa, prior caesarean/uterine surgery, advancing age and parity predispose to accreta; an unscarred uterus after vaginal delivery is not a risk factor.
NACO screens high-risk groups, promotes safe sex education and provides free treatment including for pregnant women; adoption is under CARA.
Commonest obstetric palsy is unilateral foot drop (lower motor neuron) from compression/stretch of the lumbosacral trunk by the fetal head.
Hallucinations and delusions indicate postpartum psychosis; blues shows tearfulness, anxiety, insomnia, low mood and negative feelings toward the baby.
Down syndrome newborns show brachycephaly, upslanting palpebral fissures with epicanthic folds, small ears and single palmar crease.
ICMR pregnancy guidance: no evidence SARS-CoV-2 is teratogenic; COVID-19 is not an indication for MTP and no proven increase in early pregnancy loss.
ICMR guidance: pregnant women with congenital or acquired heart disease are at highest risk; pneumonia not more severe, virus not shown in vaginal secretions or breast milk.
Blastocyst implantation begins about day 6 after fertilization (day 20 of a 28-day cycle); morula enters uterus day 4, embedding completes by day 10-11.
Partograph charts time hourly, FHR half-hourly, cervical dilatation/descent, contractions, pulse, BP, temperature, urine; maternal respiratory rate is not charted.
Active genital herpes contraindicates vaginal delivery and hence induction; postmaturity, IUGR and PROM are indications for induction.
Intracervical dinoprostone (PGE2 0.5 mg) gel is the standard gold-standard pharmacological ripening agent; oxytocin does not ripen the cervix.
In non-lactating mothers menses return by 6 weeks in about 40% and by 12 weeks in about 80%; ovulation can occur as early as 4 weeks.
Lactational amenorrhoea method: exclusive breastfeeding with amenorrhoea gives about 98% protection for the first 6 months postpartum.
Frequent effective suckling sustains prolactin and milk output; infrequent suckling, puerperal anxiety/depression and ergot prolactin suppression cause lactation failure.
Lithium for manic-depressive puerperal psychosis is excreted in breast milk, so breastfeeding is contraindicated; chlorpromazine, estradiol and ECT do not preclude it.
Erythema toxicum is a benign self-resolving neonatal rash; Mongolian spots persist beyond infancy; irritant diaper rash spares folds. Some texts call milia sebaceous plugs, creating ambiguity.
Expressed breast milk keeps 24 h refrigerated at 4°C; room temperature only a few hours. Freezer limit varies by source (3 vs 6 months), so A is debatable.
Symmetrical early-onset FGR: proportionately small fetus with normal HC:AC, FL:AC and ponderal index; raised HC/AC and low ponderal index indicate asymmetric FGR.
Growth-restricted neonates develop hypoglycaemia (poor glycogen stores), hypothermia, hypocalcaemia, polycythaemia and asphyxia; hyperglycaemia is not a recognised complication.
Augmentation stimulates existing inadequate contractions (true); PGE2 is the main cervical ripening agent (true); ripening does not explain the definition of augmentation.
Misoprostol induction can cause uterine tachysystole/hyperstimulation, meconium-stained liquor, FHR changes and rupture; water intoxication is an oxytocin effect.
Vaccines under special circumstances for high-risk children include JE, influenza, meningococcal, cholera, rabies, yellow fever and pneumococcal polysaccharide; other options say 'only'.
Kernicterus is caused by free (albumin-unbound) lipid-soluble unconjugated bilirubin crossing the blood-brain barrier and staining basal ganglia; conjugated bilirubin does not.
Pathological neonatal jaundice: onset within 24 h, bilirubin rise >5 mg/dL/day or >0.2 mg/dL/h, prolonged course or conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia.
Cardiac output rises immediately after delivery (uterine autotransfusion) and returns to non-pregnant level over about a week, so 'unchanged' is false; other statements true.
Repeated vaginal examinations introduce organisms into the genital tract and are a recognised risk factor for chorioamnionitis and puerperal sepsis.
Cracked nipple results mainly from trauma due to incorrect attachment, plus poor hygiene, retracted nipple and Candida or S. aureus infection.
In mastitis breastfeeding continues with correct attachment; starting on the unaffected side aids let-down while the affected breast is emptied; stopping feeds promotes abscess.
Brain sparing: hypoxic cerebral vasodilatation raises MCA end-diastolic velocity (low MCA PI); absent umbilical EDV and venous pulsations reflect placental insufficiency/decompensation.
Small (<5 cm) non-expanding puerperal haematomas are managed conservatively with cold compress and analgesia; large or expanding ones need evacuation under anaesthesia.
B, C, D are false (commonest cause is atonic uterus; 'always'/'never'). A is best by elimination, though most guidelines define retained placenta at 30 minutes.
Puerperal sepsis is mainly uterine infection (endometritis/endomyometritis/endoparametritis); retained products are a risk factor, not the explanation; assertion-reason judgement somewhat subjective.
Growth-restricted newborns have scanty subcutaneous fat, dry wrinkled skin, scaphoid abdomen, thin cord and alert look; fat around shoulders suggests macrosomia of diabetic mother.
OASIS classification: 3a <50% EAS, 3b >50% EAS, 3c EAS and IAS; fourth degree additionally involves the anal (anorectal) epithelium.
In reproductive years oestrogen-primed glycogen-rich epithelium supports Doderlein's lactobacilli, producing lactic acid that keeps vaginal pH about 4-4.5, the main defence.
PID is upper genital tract infection: endometritis, salpingitis, oophoritis, tubo-ovarian abscess, pelvic peritonitis; cervicitis is lower genital tract and excluded.
Gonococcus and Chlamydia trachomatis are the primary sexually transmitted causes of acute PID, roughly 30% each; the other options are secondary or polymicrobial organisms.
CDC outpatient PID regimen: single IM dose of ceftriaxone plus doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days, with or without metronidazole.

Admission criteria: pregnancy, tubo-ovarian abscess, severe illness or high fever, HIV/immunodeficiency (older criteria), failed oral therapy. Low-grade fever with mild pain is treated as an outpatient.
Rifampicin metabolites turn urine, tears and sweat orange-red.
Salpingitis gives bilateral lower abdominal pain with higher fever. Appendicitis pain starts near the umbilicus and moves to the RIF, and vomiting is more typical of appendicitis.
The etonogestrel implant has the lowest failure rate (about 0.05/100 woman-years), below LNG-IUS (about 0.2), Cu-T 380A (about 0.6-0.8) and DMPA.
Current breast cancer is WHO MEC category 4 for LNG-IUS. Mild dysmenorrhoea, age over 35 and the postpartum period are not absolute contraindications.
The Pomeroy technique (a loop of tube ligated with absorbable suture, then excised) is the most widely used tubal sterilization method.
Migraine with aura (focal neurological symptoms) is WHO MEC category 4 for combined pills because of ischaemic stroke risk. Uncomplicated diabetes is category 2.
Salpingectomy reduces tubal-origin serous ovarian/peritoneal cancer. The saline bleb is Uchida, interval ligation is done in the proliferative phase, and Pomeroy failure is about 0.1-0.5%.
Venous thromboembolism is a major, serious complication of combined pills. Mastalgia, breakthrough bleeding and chloasma are minor side effects.
Ranitidine does not induce hepatic enzymes. Rifampicin, phenytoin and barbiturates induce CYP enzymes and lower oral contraceptive efficacy.
Antara is the Government of India programme name for injectable DMPA 150 mg IM, given every three months.
Early syphilis (primary, secondary, early latent): benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. The weekly x3 schedule is for late latent disease.
The groove sign (inguinal ligament separating enlarged inguinal and femoral nodes) is characteristic of lymphogranuloma venereum, caused by C. trachomatis L1-L3.
Clue cells exceeding 20% of epithelial cells is the key Amsel criterion for bacterial vaginosis; giant cells suggest herpes, safety-pin bodies donovanosis, corkscrew organisms syphilis.
Centchroman is contraindicated in polycystic ovarian disease, cervical hyperplasia, recent jaundice/liver disease, TB and renal disease. Ormeloxifene is used to treat DUB.
Donovan bodies (intracytoplasmic Klebsiella granulomatis in macrophages, with bipolar safety-pin staining) are pathognomonic of granuloma inguinale.
A postpartum IUCD is inserted post-placentally within 10 minutes, or within 48 hours. Insertion between 48 hours and 4-6 weeks is avoided.
Quinacrine, Adiana and Essure are transcervical tubal occlusion methods. Nestorone is a progestin used in vaginal rings and gels, not a sterilization method.
Invasive cervical cancer, pulmonary TB and Burkitt lymphoma are CDC AIDS-defining conditions. Vulvar condylomata acuminata are not.
Only ZDV+3TC for 28 days is a PEP regimen here (the older basic regimen). Current NACO advises TDF+3TC+DTG for 28 days, and high-risk exposure needed three drugs.
A biological false-positive VDRL is classically seen in pregnancy and in autoimmune disease such as SLE (anticardiolipin/antiphospholipid antibodies).
Centchroman (ormeloxifene) 30 mg is taken twice weekly for the first 3 months, then once weekly.
WHO 2007 typical-use 12-month rates: female condom 21, male condom 15, LAM 2, diaphragm with spermicide 16. Only the female condom pair is correct.
Ultrasound finds an intrauterine IUCD but misses devices among bowel loops. A plain abdominal X-ray detects a radio-opaque device in the abdominal cavity. Option D's wording is odd.
Irving method: the medial tubal stump is buried in a myometrial tunnel in the posterior uterine wall, and the distal stump in the mesosalpinx.
Uchida technique: saline-adrenaline injected subserosally balloons the mesosalpinx, a tubal segment is excised and the proximal stump is buried in the mesosalpinx.
Chlamydia trachomatis is an obligate intracellular gram-negative bacterium. Serotypes D-K cause genital infection and can ascend to cause PID.
Amsel criteria: homogeneous grey discharge, pH >4.5, positive whiff test, clue cells >20%. Gardnerella culture is not a criterion.
The stem has no numbered list and no X/Y/Z column, so the coded options cannot be checked. LNG 1.5 mg and ulipristal 30 mg single doses are correct.
Puerperal tubectomy is ideally done 24-48 h after delivery (within the first postpartum week); post-placental insertion within 10 minutes refers to PPIUCD.
Ormeloxifene is used for DUB, benign breast disease/mastalgia, breast cancer and endometrial hyperplasia; polycystic ovarian disease is a listed contraindication.
Barium sulphate impregnation makes the Cu-T 380A polyethylene frame radiopaque for X-ray localisation.
HPV genital warts are treated with cryotherapy, imiquimod, podophyllin, TCA or excision; benzathine penicillin treats syphilis, not warts.
Prepubertal vagina lacks oestrogen, glycogen and Doderlein bacilli, so its pH is neutral to alkaline (about 6-8).
TSS major criteria: fever >=38.9 C, hypotension (SBP <90 mm Hg), diffuse macular erythroderma, desquamation; vomiting/diarrhoea, myalgia and disorientation are minor multisystem criteria.

Obesity causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, raised oestrogen via aromatisation and needs higher gonadotropin doses; free testosterone falls with BMI in men (rises in women), so stem is sex-ambiguous.
Upper-tier (minor) uterine supports are endopelvic fascia, round and broad ligaments; Mackenrodt's is middle tier; levator ani and urogenital diaphragm are inferior tier.
Three-swab test: urine-soaked but dye-free upper swab means urine bypasses the bladder, i.e. ureterovaginal fistula; dye-stained swabs indicate vesicovaginal fistula.
In POP-Q, total vaginal length is measured with point C/D reduced to its normal position; all other measurements are taken at maximal Valsalva.
SUI results from bladder-neck/proximal urethral descent out of the intra-abdominal pressure zone, so straining fails to raise urethral pressure; detrusor overactivity causes urge incontinence.
Subnuclear glycogen vacuolation, appearing about 36-48 hours after ovulation, is the earliest endometrial histological evidence of ovulation.
Prolapse in early pregnancy is managed by reposition and a ring pessary until about 16-18 weeks, when the uterus becomes abdominal; no surgery or termination.
Laparoscopic chromopertubation (dye test) is the gold standard for tubal patency and also shows peritubal adhesions and endometriosis.
Middle tier (cardinal/Mackenrodt's, uterosacral, pubocervical ligaments, pericervical ring) is the strongest support of the uterus.
Post-operative VVF noticed early: continuous bladder drainage with an indwelling catheter may close a small fistula; if not, delayed repair (about 3 months).
Letrozole, an aromatase inhibitor, induces ovulation without clomiphene's antiestrogenic effects on cervical mucus and endometrium.
Congestive (secondary) dysmenorrhoea: dull pain begins 3-5 days before menses and is relieved with the onset of bleeding.
Mucopurulent cervicitis: yellow mucopus on a white swab plus >=10 PMNs per oil-immersion field on Gram stain; >=5 PMNs is the urethritis cut-off.
Gonococcal salpingitis spreads along mucosa, is bilateral and closes the abdominal ostium by indrawn fimbriae (pyosalpinx); lymphatic spread and post-abortal origin are pyogenic.
Chronic uterine inversion is confused with fibroid polyp, prolapse and fungating cervical growth; Gartner's cyst is a differential of cystocele.
SSG uses saline and HSG transcervical contrast (true); falloposcopy, not salpingoscopy, views the entire tubal length; HSG is done day 7-10, not 21-23.
Pyogenic (post-abortal/puerperal) salpingitis spreads via lymphatics and veins and may be unilateral; gonococcal spreads along mucosa and is bilateral.
Hyperprolactinaemia from a prolactinoma is treated with dopamine agonists (cabergoline, bromocriptine), which restore ovulation.
Posterior compartment prolapse causes obstructed defaecation, constipation, straining, need for digitation and faecal incontinence, so all options apply.
Leiomyoma (fibroid) is the most common benign solid tumour in women; serous cystadenoma and dermoid are cystic ovarian tumours.
Ulipristal acetate is the SPRM used to reduce fibroid bleeding; mifepristone is an antiprogestin, danazol an androgen, goserelin a GnRH agonist. Option D carries a section heading.
FIGO 2014: IC1 surgical spill, IC2 capsule ruptured before surgery or tumour on ovarian surface, IC3 malignant cells in ascites or washings.
Brenner tumour shows Walthard-like transitional cell nests with coffee-bean nuclei in fibrous stroma; Call-Exner = granulosa, psammoma = serous, signet ring = Krukenberg.
A multiparous woman with dysmenorrhoea, menorrhagia and a uniformly enlarged, boggy, tender uterus has adenomyosis.
Late menarche is not a recognised CIN/cervical cancer risk factor; early first pregnancy, multiparity and smoking are. Option D carries a stray section header.
WHO: girls 9-14 get two doses; >=15 years and immunocompromised/HIV three doses. The 2022 update allows fewer doses for >=15 but keeps three, where possible, for immunocompromised.
Bivalent Cervarix covers oncogenic HPV 16 and 18; quadrivalent Gardasil adds types 6 and 11.
The progestogen in combined oral contraceptives opposes oestrogen and protects the endometrium; obesity, diabetes and tamoxifen increase hyperplasia risk.
Squamous metaplasia in the transformation zone is most active at menarche, first pregnancy and high-oestrogen states, driven by acidic vaginal pH.
Deep stromal invasion (outer third), size >=4 cm, LVSI and nodal spread are adverse factors; small tumours, absent LVSI and squamous histology are not.
VIA uses 3-5% acetic acid (acetowhite lesions); VILI uses Lugol's iodine. Option D carries a stray section header.
Endometrial cancer incidence is higher in white women, but in India cervical cancer is the commonest genital malignancy, so the reason is false.
Endometrioid adenocarcinoma (type I, oestrogen-dependent) forms about 80% of endometrial cancers.
ER/PR-positive tumours have better prognosis; aneuploidy, positive peritoneal cytology and grade 3 are adverse. Option D carries a stray section header.
Choriocarcinoma spreads haematogenously to lungs, giving cannon-ball shadows on chest X-ray; snowstorm appearance is the classic ultrasound sign of hydatidiform mole.
Salpingectomy removes the tubal origin of high-grade serous carcinoma and blocks retrograde menstruation linked to endometrioid cancer; mucinous, germ cell and stromal tumours are unaffected.
PSTT secretes little hCG and is relatively chemoresistant, so hysterectomy is the treatment of choice; the reason explains the assertion. Option D has stray header.
Cryotherapy, laser vaporisation and thermal coagulation are ablative; LEEP/LLETZ and cone biopsy are excisional treatments for CIN.
In premenopausal women with endometrial hyperplasia, persistent anovulation causing unopposed oestrogen stimulation is the constant finding.
Intramural (interstitial) fibroids are commonest (~75%), followed by subserous and submucous; cervical fibroids are rare.
EMA-CO: day 1 etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin D; day 2 etoposide, actinomycin D; day 8 cyclophosphamide and vincristine (Oncovin).
Dysgerminoma is the commonest malignant ovarian germ cell tumour and is radiosensitive, but radiosensitivity does not explain its frequency.
Thecoma is an oestrogen-secreting sex cord-stromal tumour of postmenopausal women, often causing endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma.
Red (carneous) degeneration, typically in pregnancy, gives a soft purple-red fibroid with a fishy odour attributed to fatty acids.
A pathologically enlarged ovary is a therapeutic indication; BRCA carriage, familial colonic cancer and prior breast cancer are prophylactic oophorectomy indications.
Danazol is the antigonadotropin; ulipristal and mifepristone are progesterone receptor modulators, cetrorelix a GnRH antagonist.
Asymptomatic fibroids under 12 weeks' size with a certain diagnosis are managed expectantly with six-monthly review.
Endometrial hyperplasia is commonest perimenopausally, when anovulatory cycles cause unopposed oestrogen stimulation, so the reason explains the assertion.
Pap smear, VIA/VILI and HPV DNA testing are screening tests; endocervical curettage is a diagnostic procedure.
Ganirelix (like cetrorelix) is a GnRH antagonist; goserelin, nafarelin and buserelin are GnRH agonists.
Mucinous cystadenoma is lined by a single layer of tall columnar mucin-secreting cells with basal nuclei (picket-fence pattern).
Standard texts give serous cystadenoma the highest malignant potential of these; mucinous about 5-10%, dermoid about 1-2%; functional cysts are not premalignant.
Reported ovarian cancer risk reduction after salpingectomy varies widely between studies; the 34% figure appears source-specific rather than standard textbook fact.
Late menopause, PCOS and insulin resistance increase oestrogen exposure; multiparity is protective, so only 1, 2 and 3 are risk factors.
FIGO criteria: post-molar GTN if hCG plateaus (±10%) over four values for 3 weeks or longer, or rises >10% over three values across 2 weeks.
Endometrioid adenocarcinoma accounts for about 75-80% of endometrial cancers; serous and clear cell are uncommon type II tumours.
Combined OC use roughly halves endometrial cancer risk, protection persisting years after stopping; 50% is the standard textbook figure, though duration-dependent estimates vary.
Transformation-zone squamous metaplasia is most active in fetal life, adolescence/menarche and first pregnancy, promoted by acidic (low) vaginal pH.
Pap smear, VIA and primary HPV testing are screening tests; colposcopy-directed biopsy is diagnostic. Option D carries an appended section heading; stem numbering lost.
Severe hyperemesis can cause Wernicke's encephalopathy, jaundice/hepatic failure, vitamin K-deficiency hypoprothrombinaemia, and convulsions/coma, so all four apply.
Live vaccines such as MMR are contraindicated in pregnancy; COVID-19, hepatitis B and rabies vaccines may be given.
First-trimester combined test = nuchal translucency + free beta-hCG + PAPP-A; MSAFP is a second-trimester marker. Greek letters lost from stem.
Colostrum has more protein (immunoglobulins), vitamin A, sodium and chloride, but less fat, lactose and potassium than mature milk.
Reactive NST indicates fetal well-being; NST links FHR accelerations (not breathing) to movements, begins ~30-32 weeks. Statement 3's 50% is the false-positive rate; A by elimination.
WHO: where measles transmission is low (near elimination), MCV1 may be given at 12 months for higher seroconversion; 9 months where transmission is high.
A scratch with bleeding is a transdermal Category III exposure: wound washing, anti-rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin.
Vi polysaccharide is a single SC/IM dose; Ty21a is three capsules on alternate days (1, 3, 5); protection starts about 7 days later. Only statement 1 correct.
Mantoux: 1 TU PPD in 0.1 ml intradermally with a tuberculin syringe, bevel upward, raising a 6-10 mm wheal; statements 1 and 4 correct.
Triangle of doom: vas deferens medially, gonadal/spermatic vessels laterally, peritoneal reflection inferiorly; the inferior epigastric artery bounds Hesselbach's triangle instead.
Needle-stick injuries most often involve the non-dominant index finger; washing under running water, reporting every injury and HBV/HIV testing are correct.
SIRS is driven by cytokine excess (TNF, IL-1, IL-6), iNOS nitric oxide overproduction and free radicals; microvascular occlusion is a downstream consequence, the intended exception.
Phrynoderma is attributed to essential fatty acid (chiefly linoleic acid) deficiency, not arachidonic acid; options C and D say the same thing and D carries a tick.
Egg protein is the reference protein (highest biological value/NPU) against which protein quality is assessed (Park).
Conjunctival xerosis (X1A) is the first clinical sign of vitamin A deficiency; night blindness is the earliest symptom; Bitot's spots appear later.
ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA for magnesium is 440 mg/day for adult men (ICMR 2010: 340 mg); 140 mg is far too low.
Obligatory iron loss in a healthy adult (gut, skin, urine) is about 1 mg/day, roughly 14 micrograms/kg.
Fluoride 0.5-0.8 mg/L is optimal; dental fluorosis occurs above 1.5 mg/L and skeletal fluorosis at 3-6 mg/L (Park).
Calcium per 100 g: buffalo milk 210 mg, goat 170 mg, cow 120 mg, human 28 mg (Park's milk composition table).
Human milk has less protein (about 1.1 vs 3.2 g/100 ml) and more lactose (about 7.4 vs 4.4 g) than cow's milk.
ICMR-NIN 2020 reference man is 19-39 years and 65 kg (woman 55 kg); the 2010 definition was 18-29 years, 60 kg, so option A fits neither.
Lathyrus sativus (khesari dal) causes neurolathyrism; argemone oil causes epidemic dropsy, Claviceps (ergot) ergotism, and Crotalaria veno-occlusive disease.
Park lists vitamin A prophylaxis, nutritional anaemia prophylaxis and IDD control under the Health Ministry; SNP, Balwadi and ICDS under Social Welfare.
Current MDM/PM-POSHAN primary norm is 450 kcal and 12 g protein; option C (300 kcal, 8-12 g) is the superseded 2004 norm; option D contains chatbot text.
Eradication is the absolute, all-or-none termination of transmission by extermination of the infectious agent; elimination is regional interruption of transmission.
Standard epidemic-investigation sequence begins with verification of diagnosis, then confirming the epidemic exists, defining population at risk, and case search.
Incidence guides control action; rising incidence suggests ineffective control programmes; fluctuations suggest change in aetiology (agent, host, environment). All three statements correct.
Cross-over design is unsuitable if the drug cures the disease, works only at certain disease stages, or the disease changes radically during the study.
OPV is the most heat-sensitive and hepatitis B among the least; after OPV and IPV, BCG ranks above hepatitis B, giving option D.
Statements 2 and 3 are reuse conditions under OVP; reconstituted BCG, measles and JE vials are never carried to the next session. Only option C fits.
Incidence counts only new cases in a defined population over a specified period and must state the time unit; new plus old cases defines prevalence.
Known BCG complications: suppurative lymphadenitis, osteitis/osteomyelitis and disseminated BCG infection; Guillain-Barre syndrome is not a BCG reaction.
SMR = observed/expected deaths x 100; the age-specific data are only in the unseen table image, so the explanation's 30/25 = 120 cannot be checked.
Under steady-state conditions, prevalence equals incidence multiplied by mean duration of disease (P = I x D).
Hepatitis B, pentavalent and full-dose IPV are intramuscular; BCG (and fractional IPV) are intradermal, excluding every option containing 1.
Uses of epidemiology include historical study, syndrome identification and searching for causes; making an individual clinical diagnosis is a clinical, not epidemiological, function.
Malaria is vector-borne through female Anopheles bites, not contagious; scabies, trachoma and leprosy spread by contact.
Standard PSM teaching: in the primary response, the antigen dose needed to induce IgG is about 50 times that needed for IgM.
Susceptible contacts are the 3 other children (parents immune); 2 cases give SAR 2/3 = 66.6%. Day-3/day-5 onset conflicts with measles incubation.
Analytical studies, case-control (odds ratio) and cohort (relative risk), are used to identify risk factors and estimate the degree of risk.
Attributable risk % = (Ie - Iu)/Ie x 100; the incidence data are only in the unseen image, so 62.5% cannot be verified.
Community-level priority goes to the exposure with higher population attributable risk; table unseen, but the explanation states exposure A has higher PAR.
Case-control design suits rare outcomes with long latency, such as cancer, assessing past exposure efficiently and yielding an odds ratio.
Rising incidence may indicate failure of current programmes and need for a new one, improved reporting practices, or changed aetiology; all three are correct.
PMSMA (2016) gives a fixed-day, free, assured antenatal care package on the 9th of every month.
Park's stillbirth rate counts foetal deaths weighing 1000 g or more (about 28 weeks gestation) per 1000 total births.
Haemorrhage is the leading cause of maternal deaths in India (about 38% in SRS data). The stored explanation is only a heading.
Raised amniotic fluid AFP indicates open neural tube defects such as anencephaly and spina bifida.
The 10% correction allows for pregnancy wastage (abortions, stillbirths), not under-registration. Statement II is true but does not explain Statement I.
Birth weight, gestational age and maternal education determine neonatal mortality. Adolescent mothers have higher, not lower, neonatal mortality, so statement 4 is false.
WHO: late maternal death is a death from obstetric causes more than 42 days but less than one year after termination of pregnancy.
The Apgar observations are only in the missing images, so the score cannot be calculated from the stem.
ARI table: 12 months to 5 years (10-19 kg) takes 3 paediatric cotrimoxazole tablets twice daily. Current IMNCI prefers amoxicillin.
A growth chart is a tool for action that guides the health worker's intervention, not a tool for action against the Anganwadi worker.
A flattening or falling weight curve signals growth failure, the earliest sign of protein-energy malnutrition.
Park, WHO and MoHFW IYCF guidance: start breastfeeding within one hour of birth. Older texts (original BFHI) said within half an hour.
Park/NVBDCP: DDT is the insecticide of choice for indoor residual spraying. Malathion and synthetic pyrethroids are the alternatives.
The kit pairs to be matched are only in the missing image, so the number of correct pairs cannot be checked.
SUMAN (2019) aims for zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths, with zero tolerance for denial of services.
A facility is declared an FRU for emergency obstetric surgical care, newborn care and 24-hour blood storage. Immunization is not a determinant.
NLEP ASHAs bring suspected cases to the PHC and follow up confirmed cases until treatment ends. Surgery incentives and MCR footwear come from the programme.
AB-PMJAY is jointly funded by the Centre and the States (60:40, or 90:10 for north-eastern and Himalayan states).
Under the Vande Mataram scheme, obstetricians, lady doctors and MBBS doctors volunteer safe-motherhood services and display the scheme logo.
NRC guidelines: the AWW visits weekly for the first 4 weeks after discharge, then every 2 weeks until the child leaves the programme.
NSSK trains health personnel in basic newborn care and resuscitation (hypothermia, infection, early breastfeeding) for every delivery point. All three statements are correct.
MVA makes safe early abortion available at PHCs, which reduces abortion-related maternal mortality.
Pasted page of several questions; post-LP headache is postural, relieved by lying (1, 3 true; 2 false), but '1 and 3 only' isn't offered and options cite absent statement 4.
S. pneumoniae is the commonest cause of acute suppurative otitis media. The stem does not say acute or chronic, and CSOM is mainly Pseudomonas or S. aureus.
Cataract causes painless, gradual visual loss, not an acute red eye. Keratitis, episcleritis and acute angle-closure glaucoma do.
Symmetrical depigmented patches that Wood's lamp accentuates, with autoimmune thyroiditis, indicate vitiligo. Options B and D name the same disease.
A delusion is a false, fixed belief not open to reasoning and out of keeping with the patient's sociocultural background. A describes hallucination, B illusion, C obsession.
Long-term lithium causes weight gain, hypothyroidism and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Weight loss is not a recognised effect.
Frozen shoulder affects middle-aged women, is linked to diabetes and thyroid disease, and resolves by itself over 1-2 years. Radiographs are normal, so statement 3 is false.
The Ponseti order is CAVE: cavus, then forefoot abduction (adductus), then hindfoot varus, then equinus corrected after Achilles tenotomy.
Wolff's law: bone deposition and resorption follow the mechanical stresses placed on the bone. Option C misstates the Hueter-Volkmann principle.
Ganglion is the commonest hand swelling, dorsal/volar wrist, transilluminates; seed ganglion arises from flexor tendon sheath at finger base, not DIP (that is mucous cyst).
Middle ear mucosa is supplied by the tympanic plexus, chiefly the tympanic (Jacobson's) branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve.
OME is a non-infected effusion, commoner in winter, from Eustachian tube dysfunction; management is watchful waiting or grommets/adenoidectomy, not systemic antibiotics.
Aminoglycosides, loop diuretics (frusemide) and cisplatin are classic ototoxic drugs; metronidazole is not recognised as ototoxic.
Warthin's tumour: second commonest benign salivary tumour, older male smokers, almost only parotid, bilayered oncocytic epithelium in lymphoid stroma; all four statements true.
Antrochoanal polyp is a benign maxillary antral polyp extending to the choana/nasopharynx; it is pale and avascular, unlike angiofibroma.
Folic acid supplementation, penicillin prophylaxis and LMWH thromboprophylaxis are recommended in pregnant women with sickle cell disease; azathioprine has no role.
Infants of diabetic mothers develop hypoglycaemia, hyperbilirubinaemia and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; they get hypocalcaemia, not hypercalcaemia.
Intrapartum intravenous penicillin G is the first-line agent for GBS; ampicillin is an alternative, with cefazolin, clindamycin or vancomycin reserved for penicillin allergy.
Bronchoconstrictors (opiates, PGF2-alpha, ergometrine) are avoided in asthmatic women in labour; PGE1 (misoprostol) is safe, so 1, 2 and 4.
Malaria in pregnancy causes thrombocytopenia, hypoglycaemia and DIC; the acid-base disturbance is metabolic (lactic) acidosis, not alkalosis.
Beta-thalassaemia shows low MCV/MCH, normal or raised iron indices and HbA2 >3.5%; statements 1 and 3 are certain and only option D contains both.
Highest-risk group (25-50% mortality): pulmonary hypertension and coarctation with valvular involvement; ASD is low risk and mitral stenosis intermediate.

Post-term babies risk meconium aspiration, hypoglycaemia and polycythaemia; intraventricular haemorrhage is a complication of prematurity. So 1, 2 and 4 (B), not D.

FGR newborn: old-man look, alert with normal reflexes, weight deficit. Fat around the shoulders belongs to macrosomic infants of diabetic mothers, not FGR. So 1, 2 and 3.
